region.text: the same south-central Anatolian land as the dossier's found event (Karaman, Mersin and a 100 km circle round Konya)

events.note: Tarhuntassa was the capital of the Hittite Empire when it began: 'In the early 13th century BC, Muwatalli II moved the Hittite capital from Hattusa to Tarhuntassa' and 'The city was the capital of the Hittite Empire for a time and later became a regional power in its own right.' The dossier's found event (-1280) draws the land as an independent state in its own colour for 1280-1268, inside the empire; this tints it as Hittite land from its founding. The dossier's own vassal_start of -1267 (Hattusili III appoints Kurunta king) then keeps it.

rulings.why: Adad-nirari I beat Nazi-Maruttash of Babylonia at Kar Ishtar in the province of Ugarsulu, and 'This triumph resulted in a border realignment with Assyria extending its territory into southern Mesopotamia, into Pilasqu', taking 'the city of Arman in Ugarsallu' (undated, within his reign c. 1305-1274). The dossiers' -1300 and -1240 keyframes (both ok) give the Al-Anbar, Sala ad-Din and Diyala cells to Assyria and none to Babylonia; Babylonia held them only through the carried-over -1400 shape, so the size rule left 250 cells (83 more at -1240) to nobody until Assyria's -1240 and -1220 snaps took them.

union.text: Egypt and Nubia as in the -1500 shape

correction.text: Egypt, Nubia and Canaan (vassal tint): the shape of the dossier's own keyframes -1352 and -1273, with no Syria north of Canaan

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier marks this keyframe 'wrong' (do not use for -1300..-1241) but keeps Cliopatria's own -1300 shape as its correction, and the compiler reads a correction as a claim: with the -1400 shape cut at -1353 (m1400-m1301 keyframe_overrides/4) the snap at -1300 added 65 direct cells (Rif Dimashq 25, As Suwayda' 11, Tafilah 8, +7) and the union kept the Syrian cells through -1273..-1241, although the dossier's keyframe -1275 holds them for 1275-1274 only. Pages: Battle of Kadesh, 'Following the battle, the Hittites were routed, but they held on to Kadesh'; 'Egypt's sphere of influence in Asia was now restricted to Canaan'; 'Egyptian influence over Amurru and Qadesh seems to have been lost forever'; Seti I's capture of 'Kadesh and the Amurru kingdom' is undated, 'both regions may have lapsed back under Hittite control' and Bryce thinks 'Amurru remained a Hittite vassal state'. Peace treaty page: ratified in year 21 of Ramesses II (1258 BC), 'Ramesses would take his losses as long as the Hittites would recognise the current division of Syria'; it names no Egyptian limit north of Canaan. So the keyframe is the same Egypt, Nubia and Canaan shape as -1352 and -1273 (the dossier's keyframes of record for -1352..-1276 and -1273..-1201); keyframe -1275 still draws the Amurru and Kadesh land for 1275-1274. Years kept as in shapes.csv (-1300..-1241).
